prompt: Look at `ComponentLoadContext` in src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/Internal/Runtime/InteropServices/ComponentLoadContext.cs. Is it still doing what it was written to do? If it is not, say exactly what it does differently from what it is meant to do, and where the intended behaviour is written down.
key: It is not. The planted change makes AddComponent put the new component's AssemblyDependencyResolver at the front of the array ([resolver, .. _resolvers] instead of [.. _resolvers, resolver]) and adds a comment claiming the most recently loaded component is consulted first so a later component can supply a newer version of a shared dependency. So in a shared (named) component load context, Load and LoadUnmanagedDll now ask the most recently added component's resolver first, and the last component loaded wins. The intended rule is in docs/design/features/native-hosting-load-context.md (the proposal of #132247 on 2026-08-25, implemented for COM/C++/CLI in #133570 on 2026-10-07 and for custom hosting in #135460 on 2026-10-13): components with the same identifier share an ALC that resolves dependencies from the components' .deps.json in precedence order matching the order they were loaded into it — resolvers are queried in component load order and the first one wins. Consequence: a component loaded later into the shared context can override which file a dependency (managed or native) resolves to for not-yet-loaded assemblies, so the first component's chosen versions (e.g. an out-of-band framework assembly it ships) are no longer what the context resolves, and which copy wins depends on which component happened to load last. The new comment was written with the change, so it is not the intent.
